steps.what: Review observed employee performance and check context with relevant colleagues
Evaluate employee performance against role expectations and contextual evidence
Discuss performance assessment and agree development actions with the employee

tasks.design: Keep evidence interpretation, evaluation and discussion with the supervisor. Existing {OPS_SYSTEM} work results and {TALENT} assessment records support the process; production counts are not converted into an automatic employee score.
tasks.previous_blocker: Output depends on equipment, job mix, team support and circumstances as well as individual work.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing records can make evidence accessible without replacing fair contextual assessment.
tasks.still_hard: Separating individual contribution from constraints and hearing contested evidence.
tasks.human_edge: Give specific, fair feedback and agree realistic development actions.
tasks.altitude: Performance evaluation authority and contact time stay unchanged.

reach.task: Give useful evidence about a quality-related learning need
reach.learn: Objective observations and avoiding unsupported attribution

evidence.claim: Production employee evaluation requires contextual judgement rather than treating output counts as a direct measure of individual performance.

assumptions: Boundary covers supervisor evidence review, evaluation and feedback, not HR calibration or downstream employment action.

The supervisor produces contextual observations in s1; operators and systems produce existing job records during production outside this boundary with unchanged effort. Missing or disputed records require direct clarification within retained review, not a fabricated structured score.
Assessment wording and entry are fully retained in s2. No model ranking, employee monitoring expansion or structured observation feed is introduced.
Review native assessment functions before any custom tool; none is proposed.
Zero incremental upkeep because the process and data collection remain unchanged.
unknowns: Assessment policy and whether individual attribution is reliable
research_questions: Which contextual factors most often change an initial performance assessment?

already_counted.description: Evidence review, evaluation and employee conversation remain.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, net=0. Routine assessment and contested evidence retain their full review and dialogue; no assumed score-generation saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Resolve worker problems, complaints and grievances through discussion

steps.what: Confer with workers or management to understand and resolve complaints or grievances

tasks.design: Retain direct discussion and resolution with the supervisor within the existing escalation route. Existing {HCM} policy access can support the conversation, but no automatic grievance classification or resolution is introduced.
tasks.previous_blocker: Facts may be disputed and resolution depends on trust and decision authority.
tasks.enabler_now: No supported technical change removes the substantive conversation.
tasks.still_hard: Hearing both sides, recognising a power imbalance and escalating when needed.
tasks.human_edge: Listen fairly and make commitments that the responsible people can fulfil.
tasks.altitude: Resolution and escalation rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Help describe a production concern factually
reach.learn: Fact finding and the distinction between technical issues and grievances

evidence.claim: Worker grievance resolution relies on dialogue, fair fact finding and accountable decisions.

assumptions: Boundary is the supervisor's substantive discussion; formal HR investigation and other participants' time remain outside and unchanged.

The supervisor elicits accounts and circumstances during s1. No structured grievance code, verified case file or free upstream capture is assumed; unclear facts need further conversation within retained effort.
No new software is proposed. Test existing confidential case and policy access before future additions.
Zero incremental upkeep because there is no changed capture, model or process. Any formal recording is a separate measured task and earns no saving here.
unknowns: Local grievance procedure and supervisor decision limits
research_questions: Which concerns can the supervisor resolve and which require an independent escalation route?

already_counted.description: All grievance discussion and resolution work remain.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100, net=0. Simple complaints and disputed grievances retain direct discussion; no administrative baseline is invented.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Determine production standards, budgets, goals and rates

steps.what: Confirm policies, workloads, labour availability and equipment capacity for production planning
Calculate production budget and rate scenarios under the confirmed constraints
Determine feasible standards, budgets, production goals and rates and release the plan

tasks.design: Test native planning scenarios in {OPS_SYSTEM} using validated capacity and cost inputs from {ERP} and {HCM}. Formula-based scenario arithmetic is automatic; the supervisor still checks feasibility, sets targets within delegated limits and releases the exact plan.
tasks.previous_blocker: Rebuilding calculations obscures assumptions and makes scenario comparison slow.
tasks.enabler_now: Native production planning can calculate scenarios from explicit order and capacity data.
tasks.still_hard: Choosing realistic rates and budgets when capacity, safety or priorities conflict.
tasks.human_edge: Challenge unrealistic inputs and reject a mathematically feasible but impractical target.

ambition.what: Reconsider shift-level output targets when a confirmed capacity constraint changes

tasks.altitude: Less scenario arithmetic; budget and operating authority remain unchanged.

reach.learn: Capacity calculations, units and variation in actual cycle time

evidence.claim: Siemens Opcenter APS supports production scheduling linked to ERP order information, according to the digest.
Formula-based scenario arithmetic can be separated from human choice of standards and targets.

assumptions: Boundary covers aggregate target and budget scenarios, not detailed order-level requirement calculation. The same underlying arithmetic must be owned once if shared with another task.

Production planning supplies order identifier, quantity, due date and routing version; engineering supplies setup and cycle times, crew requirements and capacity units; finance supplies approved cost rates; staffing owners supply availability. Their existing records remain unchanged outside this boundary. In s1 the supervisor reconciles effective dates, units, exceptions and missing entries, including manual capture into the planning view.

No clean capacity feed is assumed. Missing or stale inputs block automatic scenarios and return to manual calculation and clarification within retained review; four incremental focal hours allow formula checks and exceptional recalculation.
Test native scenario planning first. Formulas may calculate output, cost and utilisation, but do not judge staff performance or invent productivity assumptions.
National consultation and access requirements must be checked for changed staffing-data use; this design uses capacity information without behavioural scoring.
unknowns: Native planner availability, data quality, delegated budget limits and actual scenario arithmetic share
research_questions: Can native scenarios reproduce known plans with correct units and constraints before use?

already_counted.description: Input reconciliation and target feasibility review remain.

incremental.description: Supervisor validates formulas, investigates exceptional calculations and reviews plan defects.
Engineering and finance maintain extra planning mappings and rate-version controls.

approvals.approved_version: Exact targets, standards, budget, rates, planning-input snapshot and formula version; any change voids plan release

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=75, gross=25 less four focal upkeep hours gives net=21. High assumes scenario arithmetic is fully automated on valid inputs; low assumes manual exceptions leave only four hours released. Input validation and target judgement keep their time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Calculate labour, equipment and production requirements with standard formulas

steps.what: Confirm production order quantities, routings and capacity inputs for standard formulas
Calculate labour and equipment requirements and production specifications using standard formulas
Review calculated requirements, resolve formula exceptions and release the requirement sheet

tasks.design: Configure native requirement calculations in {OPS_SYSTEM} before building custom arithmetic. Use explicit routing, quantity and capacity inputs; the supervisor validates them and checks the resulting labour, equipment and specification sheet before internal release.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated spreadsheet calculations require copying values and maintaining consistent units.
tasks.enabler_now: Standard formulas can run deterministically in existing production planning tools.
tasks.still_hard: Recognising when a standard routing no longer describes actual production.
tasks.human_edge: Challenge an unrealistic time standard and resolve an unusual setup or crew constraint.

ambition.what: Recalculate an order's resource requirements after a verified quantity or routing change

tasks.altitude: Less routine calculation; production feasibility and release responsibility stay human.

reach.task: Check the practical validity of a machine-time standard
reach.learn: Routing versions, setup allowances and dimensional checks

evidence.claim: Siemens Opcenter APS supports detailed production planning from orders linked to ERP, as described in the digest.
Standard quantity, routing-time and capacity formulas can run without a model loop.

assumptions: Boundary is detailed order-level requirement calculation and review, not goal setting, staff assignment or production execution. Shared calculations with aggregate planning must not be counted twice.

Order planners produce item, quantity, due date and unit; engineering produces routing version, operations, setup time, cycle time, crew basis and approved formula version; equipment owners produce dated available capacity. Existing production capture remains outside and unchanged. The supervisor checks, reconciles and manually enters missing fields in s1, retaining all that time.

Invalid units, missing routing versions, zero capacity or a nonstandard operation stop automatic calculation and go to manual engineering clarification. Retained s3 review and four incremental focal hours cover exceptions and recalculation; no model extracts unverified instructions into executable requirements.
Test native calculation functions first. Existing machine runtime earns no labour saving; the removed 45 percent is explicitly supervisor spreadsheet arithmetic in the E1 baseline scenario.
Additional routing-map maintenance is counted as other-role work, not free input preparation.
unknowns: Current calculation automation, routing quality, unit conventions and true manual arithmetic share
research_questions: Do native calculations match manually verified representative orders including setup, scrap allowances and capacity units?

already_counted.description: Input reconciliation and result/exception review remain.

incremental.description: Supervisor audits requirement calculations and handles additional exceptional recalculation.
Engineering maintains additional routing mappings and formula controls.

approvals.approved_version: Exact order-bound requirement sheet, quantities, routing and formula versions and capacity snapshot; any change requires renewed review

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=55, gross=45 less four focal upkeep hours gives net=41. High assumes all routine supervisor arithmetic transfers to native formulas; low assumes existing automation and exceptional routings leave only upkeep-equivalent gains. Input capture and review retain all time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Formula arithmetic can move into native planning, while production judgement, employee evaluation and grievance resolution remain with the supervisor.
reach: Work with machinists to validate routing assumptions
Help inspectors describe quality observations without unsupported employee attribution
role.ambitious_version: A supervisor who can revisit confirmed production constraints sooner and still spends the necessary time with people and on the shop floor.
